title: VPC observability Terraform module: Prometheus/Grafana/OTel/log-shipper conductor
creator: Aria Patel
description:
Summary:
Deliver a single opinionated Terraform module (TF module) that provisions a production-ready observability stack inside customer VPCs: Prometheus (metrics), Grafana (dashboards), OpenTelemetry Collector (OTel) for traces/metrics/logs aggregation, and a configurable log-shipping component (e.g., Fluent Bit -> S3/Vector/ELK). The module must be consumable for both Private (Redwood-managed control plane) and fully customer-managed on-prem pockets, support safe upgrades, and expose health gates for orchestration automation.

Background and motivation:
- Customers deploying Redwood Private require a vetted observability baseline for SLOs, incident response, and platform health.
- Existing infra pieces are fragmented across several TF modules and manual runbooks; this consolidates common patterns and hardens upgrade/rollback behavior.
- We must reduce the operational burden during upgrades and provide deterministic health checks so orchestrator automation can perform canary and bulk rollouts.

High-level goals:
- One reusable TF module: redwood/tf-vpc-observability-conductor.
- Idempotent, minimal surface area variables with sensible defaults.
- Pluggable backend sinks (S3, Vector cloud, ELK) for logs and metrics retention.
- Safe, reversible upgrade path with pre/post hooks and health probes.
- Exported outputs for Console wiring (Grafana URL, Prometheus remote_write endpoints, OTel ingestion endpoint).

Module interface (examples):
- variables: vpc_id, region, environment, prometheus_retention_days, grafana_admin_user, auth_type, otel_image_tag, log_shipper_mode, storage_sink (s3|vector|elk), enable_service_mesh_metrics (bool).
- outputs: prometheus_service_dns, grafana_dashboard_api_key, otel_ingest_endpoint, log_shipper_status_webhook_url.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Kubernetes-first: module focuses on deploying the observability stack into a customer-managed EKS/GKE/AKS cluster or our private clusters via Helm provider in TF. This avoids re-implementing chart logic in TF and keeps lifecycle consistent with infra-as-code patterns.
- Use Helm provider to deploy Prometheus Operator + Grafana and the OTel Collector Helm chart. For log shipping we provide both a native Fluent Bit helm chart and an option to configure a Vector sidecar/daemonset.
- Storage: short-term metrics retained in Prometheus with option to remote_write to long-term storage (Thanos/Vector). Logs are forwarded to customer-configured sinks; module does not own long-term retention buckets but can bootstrap S3 buckets when requested.
- Upgrade strategy: Use HelmChart resource with version pinning and canary rollouts via small-batch nodeSelector/affinity overrides. Provide a boolean "enable_rollout_guard" that gates upgrades on healthcheck passes.

Health checks and orchestration hooks:
- Readiness probes: Prometheus rules endpoint (+ /-/ready), Grafana API check (login + /api/health), OTel Collector readiness, and Fluent Bit/Vector process health.
- Custom TF null_resource hooks: pre_upgrade_check, post_upgrade_validation. Hooks run remote-exec against a control plane job that triggers smoke tests (scrape target checks, sample traces through OTel, log roundtrip test).
- Prometheus alert rules: exporter_down, scrape_latency_high, restart_rate_high. These are translated into TF-managed alertmanager snippets to ensure consistent alerting during rollouts.
- A health webhook endpoint is exposed as an output that the Redwood orchestration layer polls; returns aggregated status: OK | DEGRADED | FAILED with a timestamp and failing component list.

Upgrade and rollback plan:
- Default behavior: no automatic upgrades unless enable_rollout_guard=false.
- Canary: update module with nodeAffinity override to target 10% of nodes, wait for health checks (configurable window), then promote to 100%.
- Rollback: store previous Helm values in a TF state-managed secret (encrypted via KMS) to allow automatic rollback invocation by ops tooling.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests: terraform validate + tflint and a small plan diff smoke runner in CI.
- Integration: a test cluster in CI that runs the full deployment and executes the pre/post hooks.
- Chaos: simulate pod evictions and network egress failures to ensure health gates prevent unsafe promotions.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- Provide an import script (terraform import helpers) to migrate from existing telemetry modules to the new conductor module.
- Config mapping table documented in Confluence: link below.

Acceptance criteria (when this ticket can be closed):
- TF module published to internal registry with README and example usage.
- Helm charts and versions pinned in module variables.
- Health webhook endpoint implemented and tested.
- Canary upgrade flow exercised in staging (evidence: CI run and manual QA notes).
- End-to-end smoke tests (metrics, traces, logs) passing in staging.
- Security review completed and KMS integration configured for sensitive outputs.

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/OBS-CONDUCTOR-2025
- Example TF usage (design snippets): https://docs.redwood.internal/obs/tf-conductor-examples.md
- GitHub draft module: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-obs-module/pull/42
- Grafana dashboard templates repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/grafana-templates/tree/obs-conductor
- Risk register and migration checklist attached in Confluence doc above.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Helm upgrade may change CRD behavior for Prometheus Operator. Mitigation: pin helm chart and test CRD upgrades in a canary cluster, include manual CRD migration step in the module docs.
- Risk: Log sink misconfiguration could cause data leakage. Mitigation: default to disabled long-term sink; require explicit opt-in and KMS-backed bucket policy.

Notes for implementer:
- Prefer minimal TF modules that delegate logic to Helm/Chart values. Use provider aliases for multi-cluster consumption.
- Add a boolean 'managed_control_plane' to toggle where certain outputs are created.
- Keep secrets encrypted with kms_key_id and do not output raw passwords; expose Grafana API keys as short-lived tokens via an ephemeral-token job.

2025-02-16 — PR opened: draft module PR #42 created (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-obs-module/pull/42). Includes Helm charts and initial TF wrappers. Needs code-owner review from infra/observability.
2025-02-17 — Code review: feedback from Maya (Security) — require explicit audit logging for bootstrap S3 buckets and deny public ACLs. Added policy variables and documentation to README.

2025-02-19 — Integration: Staging run completed. Prometheus/Grafana/OTel deployed. Observability health webhook returns OK for 3/3 components. Noted flaky Grafana dashboard provisioning; follow-up ticket recommended.
